question: Under NCAA rules, a receiver controls a forward pass, touches one foot inbounds, then steps out without losing control. Is this a catch? Assume he remains upright and maintains control long enough to perform an act common to the game.

At B-40, just before the ball reaches him, defensive player number 22 shoves him in the chest with both hands, knocking him off his route and preventing him from reaching for the pass. The pass falls incomplete. No other foul occurs; the offense accepts the penalty. What is the ruling and enforcement?

While the pass is airborne, defensive player number 22 briefly places a hand on the receiver’s shoulder and turns him away from the ball. No interference or other foul occurs. Where does the receiving team put the ball in play, and may receiving-team player number 21 advance?

On an NCAA kickoff, receiving-team player number 21 gives a valid fair-catch signal while the kick is in flight. receiving-team player number 44, who gives no signal, catches the untouched kick at B-15. No foul occurs and receiving-team player number 44 does not attempt to advance. Where does the receiving team next snap?

Fourth and 8 at A-40. The kicking team lines up in a legal scrimmage-kick formation. The potential punter simulates a punt by throwing a legal forward pass high and deep beyond the neutral zone toward eligible kicking-team player number 88. At B-40, while the catchable pass is airborne and just before it arrives, receiving-team player number 22 shoves the receiver sideways with both hands, preventing him from reaching the ball. The pass falls incomplete. The contact would ordinarily constitute defensive pass interference, but there is no holding, personal foul, or other independent foul. What is the ruling and next possession?

Second and 10 at A-30, with the line of scrimmage at A-30. Offensive player number 12 advances to A-32, where his entire body is beyond the neutral zone when he releases the ball. Facing his own goal line, he throws backward relative to his body, but the ball first touches eligible offensive player number 22 at A-34, toward the opponent’s goal from the release point. Number 22 catches it and is immediately downed. There has been no change of team possession. The defense accepts the only foul. Is this a forward or backward pass, is it legal, and what is the enforcement and next down?

Second and goal at B-8. Eligible offensive player number 88 controls a legal forward pass at the edge of B’s end zone, facing back toward the field of play. His toe touches inside the end zone, then his heel comes down on the boundary line as part of the same continuous foot landing. No other body part touches inbounds first, and he retains firm control throughout. Is this a catch and touchdown, or an incomplete pass?
